keyFindings.claim: Headless Cycles baking by script works in this container and is fast.
keyFindings.detail: Blender 5.2.2 bpy, Cycles CPU, 4 vCPU: boulder EMIT/NORMAL/AO bakes at 256^2 take 1.4/0.09/0.24 s; a 99,680-face wall chunk baked to a 5,102-face low-poly mask atlas at 1024^2 (16 spp) in 12.8 s.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: An offline tools/art step can bake every arena's hero pieces in seconds, deterministically, inside CI-like sessions.

keyFindings.claim: EMIT baking from a mask shader turns any node math (AO, pointiness, normal.z, voronoi cracks) into a texture.
keyFindings.detail: Combine masks into Emission colour channels (R=value, G=cavity, B=convex), bake type='EMIT' with use_selected_to_active from hi-poly to low-poly into a Non-Color image whose Image Texture node is nodes.active.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: One bake yields all masks needed for rule-based pixel composition and per-material ramps.

keyFindings.claim: Naive downsample+quantise of a procedural albedo yields 'camouflage' noise; rule-based composition from baked masks yields hand-shaded-looking pixel clusters.
keyFindings.detail: compose.py: mask-aware 4x box downsample, auto-levelled value into 5 mid shades, cavity -> 2 shades darker, convex lip -> +1, two passes of orphan cleanup (>=3 of 4 neighbours agree), gutter dilation. Used all 7 ramp shades with 2-4 texel clusters; naive OKLab+Bayer version was noisy.
sources: local test pixelize.py vs compose.py renders
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Generate indices by rule from form masks and reuse Orbkin's RAMPS and cluster rules as the final quantiser.

keyFindings.claim: Real CC0 PBR height+AO maps (Poly Haven, ambientCG) are excellent inputs for pixel-art textures; their colour maps are not.
keyFindings.detail: Poly Haven rock_wall_08 (16-bit displacement PNG + AO JPG) -> masks R=height, G=1-AO cavity, B=height minus 12px blur -> compose.py at 64^2 and 128^2 gave clean stones with lit tops and 1-texel dark mortar using all 7 ramp shades in ~1 s. Naive downsample of the colour map gave noise. ambientCG Rock030 (low mid-scale relief) gave coarse blobs. 16-bit PNGs must be percentile-normalised (PIL convert('L') clips them).
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Generate tileable pixel tiles (walls, floors, cliffs) from CC0 height/AO maps through the shared ramp composer instead of hand-coded fBm; pick sources whose relief matches the 16 texels/unit scale.

keyFindings.claim: Scene-level AO baked with neighbours present gives the reference's tiered-rock-wall read (dark contact crevices, lit caps).
keyFindings.detail: AO distance 0.7 world units with all boulders and the floor in the bake; flat-coloured version of the same geometry read as dough. Floor needs its own ramp/rules via a material-ID mask.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Bake AO into textures of hero diorama pieces (walls, rubble, stairs) and keep runtime lights for shafts/cookie.

keyFindings.claim: Orbkin's runtime tile painter already implements good pixel-art rules; the gap is unique, form-following surfaces on organic geometry.
keyFindings.detail: textures.ts has hue-shifted 6-7-shade ramps, band-edge-only dithering, >=2-texel clusters, palette-preserving mode mips, fixed texel density; but surfaces are small repeated tiles on boxes shaded per box by a bevel.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Don't rewrite the painter; add organic hi/low meshes and baked atlases for hero pieces, keep tiles for floors/kits.

keyFindings.claim: Pixel-art colour ramps should be hue-shifted with ~10-20 degree steps and saturation peaking in the mids.
keyFindings.detail: Darks drift toward cool/purple, lights toward warm/yellow; 'straight ramps' that only change brightness look amateur; 4-9 swatches per ramp.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Existing RAMPS comply; any new materials (moss, crystals, lodge paint) must follow the same construction.

keyFindings.claim: Stylised hand-painted texturing = value base + gradient map + cavity darkening + edge highlights + top-light + small hand-paint pass.
keyFindings.detail: Practitioner breakdowns use curvature/cavity overlays, gradient maps over grey bases, blend modes; one UE4 project cites 90% procedural / 10% hand-painted.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Claude automates the 90% (masks->ramps); the owner optionally hand-paints focal props in Krita/Aseprite.

keyFindings.claim: Consistent texel density and pixel-snapped UV islands are essential for 3D pixel art; UV seams are visible in pixel textures.
keyFindings.detail: smart_project(scale_to_bounds=False, area_weight=0) keeps island scale proportional to area; Pixel Unwrapper (early alpha) maps quad grids to whole texels; seams showed as discontinuities in the boulder test.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Size atlases from surface area at 16 texels/unit; put seams in cavities; use triplanar for terrain.

keyFindings.claim: three r180 ships a TSL triplanarTexture node, but it requires WebGPURenderer; Orbkin's WebGLRenderer needs a GLSL onBeforeCompile version.
keyFindings.detail: TriplanarTextures.js (after keijiro/StandardTriplanar) blends three projections in local space; for pixel art a hard dominant-axis switch with texel-centre snapping keeps texels crisp.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Implement world-space snapped triplanar in the existing onBeforeCompile patches for floors and kit walls.

keyFindings.claim: Bake gotchas: active image node, selected+active objects, hide hi-poly for AO, Non-Color masks, Pointiness needs dense Cycles meshes, filter_width for crisp renders, pip bpy lacks Draco/meshopt.
keyFindings.detail: Observed in this container: AO blotches until hi.hide_render=True; glTF exporter logs missing Draco/MeshOptimizer libraries; Cycles default 1.5 px filter softens low-res frames.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Encode these in the bake skill's checklist so agents don't lose time on them.

keyFindings.claim: Trim sheets and tileable textures remain the efficient choice for planks, beams, stone courses and rails.
keyFindings.detail: Strips tile in one axis; avoid distinctive features inside strips; typical sheets organised in rows.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: A pixel trim sheet for the lodge (planks, beams, shelves, rails) baked from bevelled hi-poly strips.

keyFindings.claim: Academic 3D-pixel-art renderers exist (Pixelat3D 2026, RETRO 2024, Texel Splatting 2026) but without usable code; Orbkin's integer-scale low-res pipeline already covers stability.
keyFindings.detail: Pixelat3D: priority-map texture LOD + outline post-pass, 62-person preference study; Texel Splatting addresses perspective instability.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Background only; prioritise asset-side improvements over new rendering research.

techniques.name: Hi-to-low mask bake (EMIT)
techniques.why: Captures form detail (AO, curvature, cracks) the runtime painter can't know
techniques.how: Mask shader on hi-poly -> CombineXYZ(value,cavity,convex) -> Emission; bake type='EMIT', selected-to-active, cage_extrusion 0.1, Non-Color image, margin EXTEND

techniques.name: Rule-based pixel composer
techniques.why: Avoids camo noise of naive quantisation; matches existing pixel rules
techniques.how: Box-downsample 4x, auto-levels to mid shades, cavity -2 / convex +1, orphan cleanup x2, gutter dilation, RAMPS shared with runtime via JSON

techniques.name: CC0 height/AO -> pixel tile
techniques.why: Real scanned relief gives believable stone/brick/rock structure that hand-coded noise lacks
techniques.how: Fetch height (16-bit PNG) + AO via Poly Haven/ambientCG API; percentile-normalise; R=height, G=clip((0.75-AO)*2.5), B=clip((H-blur12(H)-0.04)*8); compose.py with factor = src_px/target_px; review tiled 3x3

techniques.name: Scene-level AO bake
techniques.why: Contact shadows between pieces are the key diorama cue
techniques.how: Bake with all neighbouring pieces present, AO distance ~0.5-1 unit; hide hi-poly duplicates when baking low-poly AO

techniques.name: Material-ID mask
techniques.why: One bake serves rock/dirt/moss/wood with different ramps and rules
techniques.how: Bake material index into A channel or a second image; composer selects ramp+rules per ID

techniques.name: Organic hi/low diorama pieces
techniques.why: Boxes read as crates; reference walls are boulders
techniques.how: Icosphere/cube + layered DISPLACE (clouds/voronoi, GLOBAL coords) + decimate 0.03-0.06; or sculpt on owner machine

techniques.name: Fixed texel density atlases
techniques.how: smart_project(scale_to_bounds=False, area_weight=0); atlas_px = sqrt(area*16^2/0.6); checker review

techniques.name: World-space snapped triplanar
techniques.why: No UV seams and constant density on terrain/kit walls
techniques.how: GLSL in onBeforeCompile: dominant-axis projection, uv*=texelsPerUnit/tileTexels, snap to texel centres, per-cell flips

techniques.name: Pixel decals
techniques.why: Break tiling, add storytelling (moss, cracks, chalk, puddles)
techniques.how: Alpha-tested pixel quads / DecalGeometry merged into the arena batch with polygonOffset

techniques.name: Index texture + ramp LUT
techniques.why: On-palette shading, recolouring per route/time, 4x less memory
techniques.how: Store R8 indices; shader looks up a per-material ramp row; lighting shifts index bands

techniques.name: Pixel trim sheet
techniques.why: Planks/beams/rails reused cheaply at consistent density
techniques.how: Bake a row of bevelled hi-poly strips through the same composer; UV lodge faces onto strips

techniques.name: Hand-paint polish pass
techniques.why: The last 10% of taste on focal props
techniques.how: Owner paints over committed atlases in Krita/Aseprite; keep script outputs as the base layer
